verdicts.finding: Pinned-FBT step 1 is provably wrong: floor(i*G/N) rank ranges are not FBT(N) subtrees, so the construction does not compute R_canonical(N,L). (sprs-r03-hpc-skeptic, sprs-r07-formal-soundness)
verdicts.observed: STEP 1. /home/rohit/t16scratch/step1.py reproduces all three reviewer counterexamples exactly: N=8,G=3 rank 0 owns canonical idx {0,1,2}=heap{7,8,9}, LCA=heap 1 whose leaf set is {0,1,2,3} (r03's hand derivation, exact); N=10,G=2 rank 0 owns {0..4}, LCA=heap 0 = the whole tree (r07, exact); N=100,G=8 rank 0 owns {0..12}, LCA=heap 2 (r07, exact). Wide sweep (run_sweep.py; the fast checker was cross-validated against brute force on 300 random (N,G), all agree): over ALL 44,850 pairs with 2<=N<=300, 2<=G<=N, step 1 holds on 1,217 = 2.71%. Over the paper's own 16 leaf counts with G in 2..min(N,4096) (17,304 pairs): 208 = 1.20%. SMALLEST COUNTEREXAMPLE IS N=3, G=2 (smaller than anything either reviewer found): FBT(3) has leaves heap{2,3,4}; rank 0 owns canonical idx {0,1} = heap{2,3}; LCA = root, whose leaf set is all three. Step 1 holds essentially only when N and G are both powers of two with G<=N (plus a sparse extra family of the form G=N-N/2^k). Over the paper's OWN 40 evaluated instances, step 1 holds on 32/40 and FAILS on exactly 8: (10,4),(16,5),(50,7),(100,10),(200,12),(500,32),(1500,64),(3000,128). ROOT COMPARISON. three_readings.py evaluates the composed order under the literal reading (step 2 = canonical FBT(n_r) over the rank's own leaves, step 3 = canonical FBT(G) over sub-roots) against R_can(N,L) on the campaign's leaf vector, for all 1,546 pairs with N in {8,10,16,32,50,100,128,200,500,512}, G in 2..N: THE 64-BIT ROOT DIFFERS ON 699 = 45.21% OF PAIRS, by 1-2 ulp (max 2). On the pow2-N x pow2-G subset (52 pairs, N<=1024): 52/52 exact. On the paper's own 40 instances (suite40.py): the as-written construction gives a WRONG root on 2/40 -- npow2n_tiny_ring (N=10,G=4) off by 2 ulp and npow2_med_fat (N=200,G=12) off by 1 ulp -- and coincidentally correct on the other 38. A SECOND ERROR NEITHER REVIEWER FOUND: step 3 is wrong even when step 1 HOLDS. At N=10,G=9; N=32,G=30 and 31; N=50,G=45 and 49; N=100,G=90 the ranks do own genuine FBT(N) subtrees, yet the root still differs by 1 ulp, because the quotient of FBT(N) by those subtrees is not FBT(G) unless N and G are both powers of two. Fixing step 1 alone would therefore NOT repair the construction.
verdicts.what_is_true: Step 1 is false as stated for 97.3% of (N,G) pairs; 'each rank's local reduction reduces exactly the subtree of FBT(N) rooted at the lowest common ancestor of its leaves' is not a theorem. The downstream assertion 'This preserves Claim 1 by construction: the final root is R_canonical(N,L) regardless of G or topology' is false BY DIRECT COMPUTATION on the paper's own leaf vector -- on 45% of swept (N,G) and on 2 of the paper's own 40 instances. Independently, step 3's 'log2 G-depth all-reduce ... consistent with FBT(N)'s top log2 G levels' is well-defined and correct only when N and G are both powers of two.
verdicts.consequence: The construction as printed cannot stand. Two narrowings matter. (i) MAGNITUDE: the error is 1-2 ulp, not gross. That is still total failure of a bitwise claim -- the paper must not minimise it -- but a referee's mental picture of a wildly broken recipe is inaccurate, and the repair is correspondingly small. (ii) REPAIRABILITY, VERIFIED: two repairs compute R_can EXACTLY. (a) Induced-forest: keep floor(i*G/N), but let each rank reduce the maximal complete FBT(N) subtrees inside its range and finish the residual internal nodes in FBT(N)'s own post-order -- 0 mismatches in 1,546 pairs and 40/40 on the paper's suite, but the cross-rank stage costs up to 4.6x more combines than G-1 (578 vs 127 at N=3000,G=128) and has depth log2 N, not log2 G. (b) CUT-ALIGNED, the one to print: replace step 1 by 'cut FBT(N) at level d=ceil(log2 G); the 2^d nodes at that level partition the leaves into 2^d complete subtrees; assign those subtrees to the G ranks; the cross-rank stage evaluates FBT(N)'s top d levels.' repair_sweep.py: 426/426 (N,G) pairs give exactly R_can; the cross stage is always exactly 2^d-1 combines at depth d=ceil(log2 G) -- precisely the log2 G-depth all-reduce the paper wanted; worst-case load imbalance max_rank_leaves/(N/G)=1.969, bounded by 2 because FBT(N) is depth-imbalanced by at most one level. Four-line replacement, provable in two lines (every node of FBT(N) is still computed exactly once by the same recurrence, so the multiset and dependency order of FADDs is unchanged).

verdicts.finding: pinned-FBT, the only route to practical relevance, is unimplemented but sold in the abstract. (sprs-r01-editor-scope)
verdicts.observed: main.tex:171-174 abstract: 'We further sketch pinned-FBT, a software-only export of the ABI discipline onto existing collective libraries (NCCL, MPI, oneCCL) that inherits the invariance property without adopting our fabric.' main.tex:2523-2525: 'which we describe here as a design and leave to future work to evaluate empirically'. main.tex:2556-2557: 'A prototype on top of NCCL or oneCCL is planned as a follow-up artefact.' main.tex:2762: L2 says an NCCL comparison 'would require either (a) the pinned-FBT prototype ... or (b) silicon'. grep of snapshot/companion/main.tex returns ZERO pinned-FBT occurrences -- MOVE-TO-COMPANION is available and currently unused. Typeset extent of Sec.VIII-D in paper.pdf (pdftotext -layout, lines 1337-1377): 41 typeset lines of a ~114-line two-column page = 0.36 billed pages.
verdicts.what_is_true: The abstract sells, as a named artefact alongside three production libraries, a construction that is (a) unimplemented, (b) unevaluated, (c) mathematically wrong as printed, and (d) already built, proved and measured by someone else nine months earlier. All four verified.
verdicts.consequence: The abstract sentence and the 'It is the path we would recommend for deployments' sentence must go regardless of what happens to the rest. Cheapest possible fix (delete 3 abstract lines + 2 body lines), required independently of the mathematics.

verdicts.finding: novelty-priorart: pinned-FBT was already built and evaluated -- TBIK (arXiv:2511.17826) aligns intra- and inter-GPU reduction orders through a unified hierarchical binary tree guaranteeing bit-wise identical results regardless of TP size, in Triton, in vLLM and FSDP; RepDL (arXiv:2510.09180) is adjacent; references.bib contains nothing after 2023.
verdicts.observed: arXiv API (/home/rohit/t16scratch/arxiv_meta.xml): 2511.17826 'Deterministic Inference across Tensor Parallel Sizes That Eliminates Training-Inference Mismatch', Zhang/Ding/Yuan/Liu/Mao/Xing/Liu, v1 PUBLISHED 2025-11-21T22:40Z, v2 2026-05-29. 2510.09180 'RepDL: Bit-level Reproducible Deep Learning Training and Inference', Xie/Zhang/Chen (Microsoft), 2025-10-10. Full text of TBIK v2 fetched and read (/home/rohit/t16scratch/tbik.txt). TBIK Sec.4.1: 'we impose a fixed full binary-tree reduction topology shared by local MatMul and distributed collective operations. Each partial MatMul result corresponds to a leaf node, while internal nodes perform deterministic pairwise accumulation. Because the reduction tree is fixed and does not depend on the number of GPUs, all TP configurations follow identical accumulation paths.' Sec.4.2 is a two-stage construction identical in substance to pinned-FBT steps 2-3: intra-GPU tree reduction over T_K/C tiles at depth L=log2(T_K/C), then 'a custom Tree-Based All-Reduce kernel that follows the same tree topology'. TBIK Appendix C Theorem 1: 'Let N be the total number of tiles and C be the TP size, WHERE C IS A POWER OF TWO. If the N tiles are evenly partitioned across the C GPUs', with 'assign each GPU d the contiguous tiles L_d = {k_{(d-1)M+1},...,k_{dM}}' -- literally pinned-FBT step 1's contiguous index-range partition -- and proves by induction on C that T(k_1..k_N)=T(T(L_1),...,T(L_C)). That is precisely the theorem the SPRS paper asserts 'by construction' without proof, and TBIK states the hypothesis (2^t leaves, C a power of two) under which it is actually true -- exactly the regime my sweep found exact (52/52 pow2 x pow2). TBIK implements it in Triton, integrates it into vLLM, FSDP and SGLang, and evaluates: Count of Unique Outputs = 1 across 12 runtime configs (TP 1/2/4/8 x BS 8/16/32), Maximum Probability Divergence strictly zero, on Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B, Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, on two GPU types; and MEASURES the cost -- 22%-63% end-to-end latency overhead vs vanilla BF16 (BIO 10-33%, TBIK alone 5-30%; tree all-reduce <=10%; tree MatMul at 63% of cuBLAS throughput). Non-power-of-two: TBIK Appendix D.1 handles T_K not a power of two only via an ad-hoc 'adaptive parameter K_first ... Although this relaxes the strict binary pattern at the first reduction level, the overall accumulation order remains invariant as long as T_K/(C*K_first) >= TP_max' -- an engineering sufficient condition, NOT a canonical tree for arbitrary N. Bibliography: snapshot/paper/references.bib has 35 entries, newest year 2023 (shah2023taccl). The classical reproducible-summation line IS cited (demmel2013reproBLAS, iakymchuk2016exblas, collange2015reproducible, rump2009accurate, kahan1965summation), so 'nothing after 2023' concerns the 2025-26 determinism wave specifically, not ignorance of the field. Also absent: Thinking Machines Lab, 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference' (Sep 2025, TBIK's ref 10); CoRun, arXiv 2026-08-14, 'Padding is Simple and Efficient for Deterministic LLM Inference'.
verdicts.what_is_true: ANTICIPATED, precisely: (1) the mechanism -- one fixed full binary tree shared by intra-rank and inter-rank reduction so the accumulation order is independent of the rank count; (2) the rank partition -- contiguous equal blocks of leaves, character-for-character pinned-FBT step 1; (3) the two-stage composition = steps 2+3; (4) the correctness theorem, PROVED, for the power-of-two case -- the only case in which pinned-FBT is correct; (5) a working implementation in production stacks; (6) an empirical demonstration of bitwise invariance across configurations; (7) a measured overhead figure for the discipline. NOT ANTICIPATED: (a) arbitrary non-power-of-two N -- TBIK's operator is defined on 2^t inputs and its K_first relaxation is not a canonical tree; SPRS's canonical FBT(N) with heap-index leaf enumeration, the depth-imbalance discipline of Def.3, and the heap-vs-visual one-ulp example at N=200 are genuinely absent from TBIK; (b) the cut-aligned repair; (c) cross-TOPOLOGY invariance -- TBIK varies TP size inside one node over NVLink/PCIe and never sweeps network topologies, so the six-direct-network 2,822-configuration result is unanticipated; (d) fabric/hardware enforcement, the compiler-fabric ABI framing, Property 2 fail-stop, the structural cost decomposition, FP64. The reviewer OVERSTATES in saying pinned-FBT 'was already built': the arbitrary-N generalisation was built by no one. But that understates the sting -- the arbitrary-N generalisation is exactly the part that is wrong. The correct part of pinned-FBT is exactly the part TBIK already proved, built and measured.
verdicts.consequence: TBIK v1 predates the snapshot (2026-08-17, MANIFEST.json) by nine months and predates every dated artefact in the repository (tables generated 2026-08-09); main.tex contains no arXiv preprint id for this work. It is PRIOR ART, not concurrent, and no priority argument is available. NEGATIVE: pinned-FBT cannot be presented as a contribution; a referee who finds TBIK will read the abstract's final sentence as a novelty claim over published work. POSITIVE and currently unclaimed: TBIK is independent third-party evidence that the ABI discipline is (i) achievable in software on commodity GPUs, (ii) worth doing -- it fixes a real RL training/inference mismatch -- and (iii) carries a measured 22-63% cost, which CORROBORATES this paper's central thesis that reproducibility must be priced structurally. Citing it converts the weakest paragraph in the paper into external validation of its thesis. Separately, a 2026 submission on bitwise-reproducible collectives whose bibliography stops at 2023 and omits the entire 2025-26 determinism literature is a standalone rejection risk that must be fixed regardless.

Strictly cheaper in pages than the status quo; removes a provably false claim rather than defending it; discharges the post-2023-bibliography risk in the same edit; turns the paper's weakest paragraph into third-party corroboration of its central thesis. headline: BOTH attacks land, the paper is worse off than either reviewer said, and yet the repair is four lines and the prior art is an asset as much as a liability. Step 1 is false: over all 44,850 (N,G) with 2<=N<=300 it holds on 1,217 = 2.71%; the smallest counterexample is N=3,G=2 (smaller than any reviewer found); it fails on 8 of the paper's own 40 instances. All three reviewer counterexamples reproduce exactly. Worse, 'the final root is R_canonical(N,L) regardless of G or topology' is false by direct FP64 computation on the paper's own leaf vector -- the as-written construction returns a different 64-bit root on 699/1,546 = 45.2% of swept pairs (1-2 ulp) and on 2 of the paper's own 40 instances (N=10,G=4 by 2 ulp; N=200,G=12 by 1 ulp). A second error neither reviewer found: step 3 is wrong even where step 1 HOLDS (N=10,G=9; N=32,G=30,31; N=50,G=45,49; N=100,G=90), because the quotient of FBT(N) by rank subtrees is not FBT(G) outside the power-of-two case -- so fixing step 1 alone would not repair it. The construction is exact precisely when N and G are both powers of two (52/52 verified). A verified four-line repair exists: cut FBT(N) at level ceil(log2 G) instead of partitioning canonical index ranges -- 426/426 pairs exact, cross stage exactly 2^ceil(log2 G)-1 combines at depth ceil(log2 G), load imbalance bounded by 2 (worst observed 1.969). On prior art: TBIK v1 (2025-11-21, nine months before the snapshot; this paper has no preprint) proves in Appendix C exactly the theorem pinned-FBT asserts without proof, under exactly the power-of-two hypotheses that make it true, using literally the same contiguous-block rank partition, and implements it in Triton inside vLLM/FSDP/SGLang with zero probability divergence across 12 TP/batch configurations and a measured 22-63% end-to-end overhead. So the correct part of pinned-FBT is the part TBIK already did; the part TBIK did not do -- arbitrary N -- is the part that is wrong. TBIK does NOT anticipate canonical FBT(N) for non-power-of-two N with heap-index enumeration, the cut-aligned repair, cross-TOPOLOGY invariance (TBIK varies TP size inside one node and never sweeps networks), fabric enforcement, fail-stop, FP64, or the structural pricing. RECOMMENDATION: cite-as-extension. Delete the abstract sentence and the three-step recipe; keep ~14 lines citing TBIK as independent corroboration -- its 22-63% measured overhead is external support for this paper's thesis that reproducibility must be priced; state the corrected cut rule in one sentence; move the proof and the sweep table to the companion, which today contains zero pinned-FBT material. Net -0.15 billed pages, and it simultaneously fixes the standalone rejection risk that references.bib ends at 2023 and omits the entire 2025-26 determinism literature (TBIK, RepDL, batch-invariant kernels, CoRun).

On the pow2 x pow2 subset (52 pairs, N<=1024) the construction is exact 52/52. Two verified repairs return R_can exactly: (a) induced-forest (0/1,546 mismatches, 40/40 on the suite, but cross stage up to 4.6x G-1 combines and depth log2 N), and (b) CUT-ALIGNED -- cut FBT(N) at level d=ceil(log2 G), assign the 2^d resulting complete subtrees to the G ranks, cross stage = FBT(N)'s top d levels -- 426/426 exact, cross stage exactly 2^d-1 combines at depth exactly d, worst load imbalance 1.969 (bounded by 2).

prior_art.anticipated: TBIK (arXiv:2511.17826v1, 2025-11-21) anticipates: the mechanism (a single fixed full binary tree shared by intra-rank and inter-rank reduction, making accumulation order independent of the rank count); the rank partition (contiguous equal leaf blocks -- literally pinned-FBT step 1); the two-stage composition (local tree reduce then tree all-reduce over sub-roots on the same topology = steps 2+3); the correctness theorem PROVED by induction in Appendix C for the power-of-two case, which is exactly and only the case in which pinned-FBT is correct; a Triton implementation integrated into vLLM, FSDP and SGLang; an empirical demonstration of bitwise invariance (Count of Unique Outputs = 1 and zero Maximum Probability Divergence across 12 TP x batch-size configurations, 4 models, 2 GPU types); and a measured cost (22-63% end-to-end vs BF16; tree all-reduce <=10%; tree MatMul 63% of cuBLAS throughput). RepDL (2510.09180, 2025-10-10, Microsoft) is adjacent: bitwise reproducible DL via correct rounding and order invariance. Thinking Machines Lab, 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference' (Sep 2025) is the batch-invariant-kernel baseline TBIK builds on. CoRun (2026-08-14) is a scheduling alternative. None of the four appears in references.bib, whose newest entry is 2023.
prior_art.not_anticipated: (1) Arbitrary non-power-of-two N. TBIK's operator T is defined on 2^t inputs and Theorem 1 requires C a power of two; non-power-of-two tile counts get an ad-hoc 'adaptive parameter K_first' that 'relaxes the strict binary pattern at the first reduction level' under a sufficient condition -- not a canonical tree. SPRS's canonical FBT(N) with heap-index leaf enumeration, the explicit depth-imbalance discipline (Def.3 and the N=200 heap-vs-visual one-ulp example), and the cut-aligned repair are genuinely not in TBIK. (2) Cross-TOPOLOGY invariance: TBIK varies TP size within a single node over NVLink/PCIe and never sweeps network topologies; the six-direct-network, 2,822-configuration invariance result is unanticipated. (3) Fabric/hardware enforcement, the compiler-fabric ABI framing, Property 2 fail-stop, the structural cost decomposition, and FP64. The reviewer therefore OVERSTATES in saying pinned-FBT 'was already built and evaluated' -- the arbitrary-N generalisation was built by nobody -- but understates the sting: that generalisation is precisely the part that is mathematically wrong.
